name: Ceramic and glass
summary: Materials that fire changes for ever: clay bodies, glazes, slips, glass, vitreous enamel, brick and tile.

materials.name: Bare clay (unglazed)
materials.summary: No glaze: the fired clay is the surface. Bizen, Yixing, terracotta and jasper ware leave it bare.
materials.photo: a square sample tile of bare clay

materials.name: Biscuit (unglazed porcelain)
materials.summary: Fired porcelain left without glaze, matte and white like marble. Vincennes and Sèvres used it for figures.
materials.photo: a small unglazed matte white biscuit porcelain figurine of a seated woman, like white marble

materials.name: Burnished
materials.summary: Clay polished with a stone or a bone before firing, so that it shines without a glaze.
materials.photo: a square sample tile of burnished

materials.name: Brick
materials.photo: a rough block of brick

materials.name: Glazed brick
materials.photo: a rough block of glazed brick

materials.name: Ceramic
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of ceramic clay body

materials.name: Black basalt
materials.summary: A black unglazed stoneware coloured with iron and manganese, made for vases and teaware in the antique style.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of black basalt clay body

materials.name: Bone china
materials.summary: A porcelain with calcined bone ash. It is white, thin and strong. Josiah Spode set the standard recipe about 1796.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of bone china clay body

materials.name: Ceramic tile
materials.photo: a square glazed ceramic tile
materials.photo_applied: a square sample of glazed ceramic tiles with grout

materials.name: Creamware
materials.summary: A cream-coloured earthenware with a lead glaze. Josiah Wedgwood refined it as Queen's ware in 1762.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of creamware clay body

materials.name: Earthenware
materials.summary: A porous body fired below about 1150 °C. Pots from Xianrendong Cave are the oldest known vessels of fired clay.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of earthenware clay body

materials.name: Egyptian faience
materials.summary: A body of ground quartz with an alkaline flux that glazes itself when it dries and fires. It is not a clay body.
materials.photo: an ancient Egyptian turquoise-blue glazed faience bead amulet

materials.name: European hard-paste porcelain
materials.summary: The first European true porcelain. The Meissen manufactory began production in 1710.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of european hard-paste porcelain clay body

materials.name: Fireclay
materials.summary: A refractory clay that resists heat and holds a large cast without warping: Belfast sinks, baths and kiln furniture.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of fireclay clay body

materials.name: Fired brick clay
materials.summary: A coarse clay fired in moulded blocks. Glazed brick makes the Ishtar Gate of Babylon, about 575 BC.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of fired brick clay clay body

materials.name: Glass-ceramic
materials.summary: A glass that heat turns into a fine crystal ceramic, so that it takes a flame and the freezer. Stookey found it by accident; Corning Ware used it from 1958.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of glass-ceramic clay body

materials.name: Ironstone china
materials.summary: A hard, heavy, white body patented as a cheap substitute for porcelain.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of ironstone china clay body

materials.name: Jasperware
materials.summary: A fine unglazed stoneware coloured with metal oxides, with white relief in the same body.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of jasperware clay body

materials.name: Paper clay
materials.summary: Clay mixed with paper fibre, so that thin sculptural forms stand and join when dry.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of paper clay clay body

materials.name: Parian porcelain
materials.summary: An unglazed biscuit porcelain that looks like Parian marble. It made figures and busts for the Victorian home.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of parian porcelain clay body

materials.name: Pearlware
materials.summary: Creamware with a little cobalt in the glaze, so that it looks whiter. It carries blue transfer prints well.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of pearlware clay body

materials.name: Porcelain
materials.summary: A white, dense and translucent body of kaolin and porcelain stone, fired at about 1300 °C.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of fired porcelain, a fine bright white body

materials.name: Porcelain stoneware (gres porcellanato)
materials.summary: A pressed tile body with water absorption below 0.5 %. It makes floor and wall tiles that copy stone, wood and concrete.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of porcelain stoneware clay body

materials.name: Pyrogranite
materials.summary: A hard, frost-proof architectural body that the Zsolnay factory developed. It makes roof tiles, relief panels and finials with a strong glaze.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of pyrogranite clay body

materials.name: Raku clay
materials.summary: An open, grogged clay that survives the shock of a hot kiln. Pieces are hand-built, not thrown.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of raku clay clay body

materials.name: Red stoneware (zisha)
materials.summary: A fine iron-rich stoneware, left unglazed. Yixing teapots in this body take a patina from tea.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of red stoneware clay body

materials.name: Soft-paste porcelain
materials.summary: A glassy body of white clay and frit, an early European imitation of Chinese porcelain. Sèvres used it until about 1770.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of soft-paste porcelain clay body

materials.name: Stonepaste (fritware)
materials.summary: A white body of ground quartz, glass frit and a little clay. Islamic potters used it to copy Chinese porcelain; Iznik ware uses it.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of stonepaste clay body

materials.name: Stoneware
materials.summary: A dense, vitrified body fired at about 1200 to 1300 °C. It holds water without a glaze.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of stoneware clay body

materials.name: Technical porcelain
materials.summary: A high-alumina porcelain for electrical insulators and laboratory ware. It resists voltage, heat and acids.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of technical porcelain clay body

materials.name: Terracotta
materials.summary: A red, iron-rich earthenware, often left unglazed. It makes figures, roof tiles and facade blocks.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of terracotta clay body

materials.name: Vitreous china
materials.summary: A dense, white body with near zero water absorption, cast for sanitary ware: basins, WCs and urinals.
materials.photo: a small unglazed test cylinder of vitreous china clay body

materials.name: Vitreous enamel
materials.summary: Glass fused onto metal; the dial of the fine watch and the colour of Art Nouveau and Art Deco jewels.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with vitreous enamel

materials.name: Back-painted glass
materials.photo_applied: a square sample of a back-painted glass splashback
materials.photo: a square sample of clear glass painted on the back an even opaque deep red, seen from the front

materials.name: Borosilicate glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of borosilicate glass

materials.name: Clear glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of clear glass

materials.name: Coloured glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of coloured glass

materials.name: Frosted glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of frosted glass

materials.name: Glass
materials.summary: A non-ceramic glassy material. It is a substitute that breaks the look of fired clay.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of glass

materials.name: Glass block
materials.photo: a rough block of glass block

materials.name: Glass pearl
materials.summary: A glass bead coated with a pearl-like layer; the base of the long ropes of costume jewellery. By tradition, the rosary maker Jaquin made the first one in 1656.
materials.photo: glass pearl

materials.name: Laminated glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of laminated glass

materials.name: Mirror glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of mirror glass

materials.name: Neon tube
materials.photo: neon tube

materials.name: Opal glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of opal glass

materials.name: Paste
materials.summary: Lead glass cut and foil-backed to look like diamond; Georgian paste was a jewel of its own, not only a copy.
materials.photo: a Georgian paste jewel brooch of clear cut lead glass stones in a silver setting that sparkle like diamonds

materials.name: Plate glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of plate glass

materials.name: Pressed glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of pressed glass

materials.name: Stained glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of stained glass

materials.name: Safety glass
materials.photo: a square sample of safety glass, the edge seen

materials.name: Tempered glass
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of tempered glass

materials.name: Alkaline glaze
materials.summary: A glaze fluxed with soda or potash. It gives bright turquoise with copper and blue with cobalt.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with alkaline glaze

materials.name: Ash glaze
materials.summary: A glaze from wood ash. In a wood kiln it forms by itself as green-brown runs on the shoulder of a pot.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with ash glaze

materials.name: Celadon
materials.summary: A green to blue-green glaze from a little iron in reduction. Longquan and Korean Goryeo celadons are the classic forms.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with celadon

materials.name: Clear porcelain glaze
materials.summary: A transparent high-fired feldspar glaze that shows the white body and underglaze painting.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with clear porcelain glaze

materials.name: Coloured gloss glaze
materials.summary: A smooth, even, saturated industrial glaze in one colour.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with coloured gloss glaze

materials.name: Copper red
materials.summary: A red glaze from copper in reduction, hard to control: sang de boeuf and flambé.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with copper red

materials.name: Crackle glaze
materials.summary: A glaze that crazes in a net of lines on cooling. Potters stain the lines to show them.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with crackle glaze

materials.name: Crystalline glaze
materials.summary: A zinc glaze that grows flower-like crystals in a slow cool.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with crystalline glaze

materials.name: Eosin glaze
materials.summary: An iridescent lustre glaze in red, purple and gold that the Zsolnay factory made. It gives roof finials and wall panels an oily metallic sheen.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with eosin glaze

materials.name: Iron brown glaze
materials.summary: A glossy brown glaze coloured by iron oxide. It covers telegraph and power insulators, because it hides soot and dirt and sheds rain.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with iron brown glaze

materials.name: Jun glaze
materials.summary: A thick opalescent blue glaze, often with purple splashes of copper.
materials.photo: a small stoneware bowl with a thick opalescent sky-blue jun glaze with a purple splash

materials.name: Lava glaze
materials.summary: A thick, bubbled glaze that looks like lava, the surface of West German Fat Lava vases.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with lava glaze

materials.name: Lead glaze
materials.summary: A clear, low-fired glaze fluxed with lead oxide. It is glossy and takes colour from metal oxides.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with lead glaze

materials.name: Victorian majolica glaze
materials.summary: Bright coloured lead glazes over moulded relief, shown at the Great Exhibition of 1851.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with victorian majolica glaze

materials.name: Matte glaze
materials.summary: A dry, velvet glaze. Grueby matte green set the surface of American art pottery.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with matte glaze

materials.name: Oribe glaze
materials.summary: A copper-green glaze poured over part of a piece, named after the tea master Furuta Oribe.
materials.photo: a small square stoneware dish with a glossy copper-green oribe glaze poured over half of it

materials.name: Raku glaze
materials.summary: A low-fired glaze on a piece pulled hot from the kiln. Black and red raku tea bowls are the canonical forms.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with raku glaze

materials.name: Salt glaze
materials.summary: Salt thrown into a hot kiln forms a thin glaze with an orange-peel texture on stoneware.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with salt glaze

materials.name: Sancai (three-colour)
materials.summary: Lead glazes in amber, green and cream that run together on tomb figures and vessels.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with sancai

materials.name: Sanitary glaze
materials.summary: A glossy, hard, white zircon glaze that cleans easily, sprayed on vitreous china and fireclay.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with sanitary glaze

materials.name: Satin glaze
materials.summary: A glaze between matte and gloss, about 20 to 50 GU, common on studio and Scandinavian ware.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with satin glaze

materials.name: Shino glaze
materials.summary: A thick white feldspar glaze with pinholes and fire-orange edges.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with shino glaze

materials.name: Soft-paste glaze
materials.summary: A soft, glassy lead glaze that fuses with the body of soft-paste porcelain. It pools in the corners and takes enamel colours well. English factories used it from about 1745.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with soft-paste glaze

materials.name: Tenmoku
materials.summary: A dark iron glaze that breaks to brown on rims. Hare's fur and oil spot are its effects.
materials.photo: a small conical tea bowl with a glossy black tenmoku glaze that breaks to rust brown at the rim

materials.name: Tin glaze
materials.summary: An opaque white lead glaze with tin oxide. It is the base of maiolica, faience and delftware.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with tin glaze

materials.name: Uranium oxide glaze
materials.summary: A bright orange-red glaze coloured with uranium oxide, the red of Fiesta ware.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with uranium oxide glaze

materials.name: Albany slip
materials.summary: A natural brown clay from Albany, New York, that melts to a dark glossy coat at stoneware heat. American potters dipped crocks and jugs in it.
materials.photo: a small stoneware jug coated with a glossy dark chocolate-brown albany slip glaze

materials.name: Attic black gloss
materials.summary: A fine iron-rich slip that turns black and glossy in a three-stage firing. It makes black- and red-figure ware.
materials.photo: a small stoneware test tile coated with attic black gloss

materials.name: Terra sigillata
materials.summary: A red gloss slip of very fine clay particles, the surface of Roman tableware.
materials.photo: a small Roman-style bowl with a smooth glossy orange-red terra sigillata surface

materials.name: Ferrite magnet
materials.photo: a dark charcoal-grey ferrite ring magnet

materials.name: Technical ceramic
materials.summary: Zirconium oxide sintered hard and polished; it does not scratch and does not fade, and watch cases and bracelets use it.
materials.photo: a polished white zirconia ceramic watch case and bracelet links, a smooth hard satin white surface
